question.text: Under the SEBI Portfolio Managers framework, deviations from the intended allotment in client portfolios are permitted:

answer.text: At the discretion of the dealer at any time
Only in exigency, with prior written approval of the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer and detailed rationale
Whenever clients verbally request, without any written record
Up to 25% of portfolio value without any approval

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI Portfolio Managers framework requires every PM to have written policies on order placement and allocation. Deviations from the intended allotment across client portfolios are not routine — they are permitted only in exigency, and even then only with prior written approval of the Principal Officer and the Compliance Officer, accompanied by a detailed written rationale. This protects clients from arbitrary allocation drift and ensures every deviation has documented internal accountability. The Trap: "Dealer discretion at any time" eliminates the supervisory check that the framework explicitly demands. "Verbal client requests without written record" violates the documentation requirement. "Up to 25% without any approval" invents a quantitative threshold that the regulations do not provide; the test is exigency + prior written approval, not a percentage. Note: This framing is drawn from the NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook treatment of order placement and allocation policies (page 142 in the cited edition), which states that deviations from the intended allotment require prior written approval of the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer with detailed rationale. The original "Material Deviation threshold for client notification" framing in earlier editions of this question is not supported by the cited workbook pages.
